cleanIntro:
The H&R AR15 is an AR-15 sold under the Harrington & Richardson name. It breaks open the usual AR way: the rear takedown pin comes out to its stop, the upper pivots on the front pin, and the bolt carrier and charging handle slide out of the back of the upper.

The book covers the H&R AR family. Its field strip and bolt carrier group sections are printed once for the family, and this guide follows them.

Two lubrication rules carry through: the chamber is left dry, and the inside of the carrier gets no oil. The book takes the bolt down as far as the extractor and stops there.

steps.title: Selector on SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard, and put the safety selector on SAFE before anything else.
steps.prose: Everything after this assumes the rifle cannot fire while you work the controls.
steps.quote: Place the safety selector on SAFE
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.18

steps.title: Magazine out — press and pull DOWN
steps.action: Hold the pistol grip with your finger off the trigger, press the magazine release button and pull the magazine straight down out of the well.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the charging handle moves; cycling with a loaded magazine in only feeds the next round.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button and pull the magazine down to remove.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.18

steps.title: Charging handle back, lower bolt catch in, bolt locked open
steps.action: Unlock the charging handle and pull it all the way back, press in on the LOWER part of the bolt catch, then let the charging handle go. The bolt stays locked open on the catch.
steps.prose: Pressing the lower part locks the bolt; the upper part releases it.
steps.quote: Unlock and pull the charging handle all the way out [figure 3] and press in on the lower portion of the bolt catch [figure 4]. Release the charging handle. This locks the bolt in the open position.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.19

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: With the bolt held open, look through the ejection port into the chamber and confirm it is empty.
steps.prose: Seeing an empty chamber is the check. Working the action is not.
steps.quote: Look into the receiver through the ejection port and verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber [figure 5].
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.19

steps.title: Rear takedown pin — push from the LEFT
steps.action: Push in the takedown pin from the left side of the receiver. It sits above and behind the safety lever.
steps.prose: This is the rear pin only. The front pin stays where it is.
steps.quote: Push in the takedown pin, located above and to the rear of the safety lever on the left hand side of the receiver [figure 15].
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Pull the pin from the right until it stops
steps.action: From the right side, pull the takedown pin out until it stops. It is captive and will not come out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Stop when it stops. Do not lever it looking for a loose pin.
steps.quote: You may then pull the pin from the right side of the receiver until it stops (it will not pull out)
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Upper pivots open on the front pin
steps.action: Hold the rear of the upper receiver and lift it, letting it pivot on the front pin. The lower's fire control group is now exposed.
steps.prose: Leave the fire control group alone — the book publishes nothing for it.
steps.quote: Grasp the rear of the upper receiver and pull up, allowing it to pivot on the front pin. This will expose the fire control group.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Bolt carrier straight back and out
steps.action: Pull the bolt carrier straight back until it comes free of the charging handle and out of the upper.
steps.prose: Straight back, no twisting. Catch it as it clears the receiver.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt carrier straight back until it is free of the charging handle and upper.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Charging handle back, drop it, out the rear
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back until it stops, let it drop down so it clears the upper receiver, and take it out of the rear.
steps.prose: It only comes out once it has dropped clear of the upper.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle back until it stops, then allow it to drop down to clear the upper receiver and remove it from the rear.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper and lower, still joined at the front pin; the bolt carrier group; and the charging handle. The book's cleaning section has you take the bolt carrier apart, and it takes the buffer and buffer spring out of the buffer tube. Both are in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes off for routine cleaning.
steps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — MAINTENANCE, printed p.30

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, firing pin out the back
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt into the carrier until it stops. Pull out the firing pin retaining pin, then slide the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Work over the bench. The retaining pin is small.
deepSteps.quote: Remove firing pin retaining pin (E) and slide firing pin (F) to the rear of the carrier until it is free.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Cam pin turned clear of the gas key, then out
deepSteps.action: Turn the cam pin until its head clears the gas key, then pull it straight out. The bolt cannot leave the carrier until the cam pin is out.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The cam pin must go back in. The book warns that without it the rifle can still fire and may explode.
deepSteps.quote: the pin to clear the gas key, and pull straight out.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt assembly out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Clean the bolt and the carrier as separate pieces from here.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt assembly may now be removed from the carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out, extractor off
deepSteps.action: Push the extractor pin out and take the extractor off the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the extractor, its pin and its spring together on the bench.
deepSteps.quote: Push extractor pin out to remove extractor.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Check the extractor spring and spacer
deepSteps.action: Note where the spring and spacer sit on the extractor and look at their condition. If either is missing or worn, replace it.
deepSteps.prose: A tired extractor spring is a common cause of failures to extract.
deepSteps.quote: Note position and condition of spring and spacer on the extractor. If items are missing or worn, replace.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Buffer tube — the buffer and spring are under load
deepSteps.action: With the upper and lower separated, the buffer and buffer spring are visible in the buffer tube. Put on eye protection before you release them.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is compressed. Keep control of the buffer the whole way.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BUFFER TUBE DISASSEMBLY, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Press the buffer retainer, let the buffer forward slowly
deepSteps.action: Hold the buffer back and push down on the buffer retainer pin. Once the buffer clears the retainer, let it come forward slowly.
deepSteps.prose: Do not let it fly out; ease it forward under your thumb.
deepSteps.quote: Push down on the buffer retainer pin [Figure 24] while holding the buffer back. Allow buffer to travel forward slowly after clearing the retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BUFFER TUBE DISASSEMBLY, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Buffer and spring out of the tube
deepSteps.action: When the spring is no longer compressed, take the buffer and buffer spring out of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.prose: The inside of the tube can now be cleaned.
deepSteps.quote: Once the spring is no longer compressed, remove the buffer and buffer spring from the buffer tube.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BUFFER TUBE DISASSEMBLY, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: This is where the book stops
deepSteps.action: The bolt carrier group is apart down to the extractor, and the buffer and spring are out. The book goes no further for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past this point is for a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No Further disassembly is required for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL — H&R AR FAMILY USERS MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — BOLT CARRIER GROUP DISASSEMBLY, printed p.27

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush with bore solvent or CLP, several passes to scrub the inside of the chamber.
Wipe with clean patches until a patch stays clean.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel several times, starting from the chamber end.
Cleaning brush through several times with more bore cleaner to lift copper fouling and powder residue.
Patch again; if it does not come out clean, brush again until a clean patch exits.
One patch with gun oil through the bore to protect it.
Outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant, then wipe clean.
Do not let the cleaning rod scratch the inside of the barrel or chamber.

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Strip per the deep-clean steps and clean with CLP or a suitable solvent.
Wipe excess oil off the bolt assembly before reassembly.
⛔ Do not lubricate the inside of the carrier — lubricate the exterior only.

cleaning.name: BUFFER TUBE
tasks: With the buffer and spring out, clean the inside of the buffer tube with a cotton patch and CLP.

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe all metal with a clean cloth, then a lightly oiled cloth.
Use only cleaning solutions made for firearms — some solvents can damage the finish.
⚠ Excess oil or grease can raise pressure dangerously and may burst the barrel when fired — keep it light.

reassembly: Buffer spring and buffer back into the buffer tube, pushed past the buffer retainer pin.
Extractor, its spring and spacer back on the bolt; extractor pin pushed back in.
⛔ Cam pin back in through its slot and turned into place. Without it the rifle can still fire and may explode.
Firing pin in from the rear, then the firing pin retaining pin back through the carrier.
Charging handle back into the upper, then the bolt carrier group in behind it.
Close the upper onto the lower and push the rear takedown pin fully home from the right.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: The book does not print a function check. With the rifle reassembled, magazine out and chamber seen empty: work the charging handle several times — the bolt should run without binding and close fully. Lock the bolt open on the lower part of the bolt catch and release it again. Make sure the takedown pin is pushed fully home. If anything binds or the bolt will not close, do not fire it; contact the maker.
